taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 480, Cercidium floridum: small tree 4-6 m. high.

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "Blue paloverde grows to 32.8 feet (10 m) tall"; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426) give the genus up to about 8 m.

traits.stem_diameter_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "with a trunk diameter of 1.5 feet (0.5 m)".

traits.crown_width_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "a crown spread of 163.4 square feet (15.2 sq m)": a round crown about 4.4 m across.

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "a native, spiny, small tree or subtree".

traits.woodiness.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "a native, spiny, small tree or subtree".

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "Its pinnately compound leaves are about 1 inch (2.5 cm) long and drought-deciduous"; "remains leafless throughout most of the year".

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 480, Cercidium floridum: a small tree with leafy branchlets, no rosette.

traits.bark_texture.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 480, Cercidium floridum: bark smooth, pale grey-green.

traits.bark_colour.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426), Cercidium floridum: young bark bluish green (FEIS: "thin-barked, photosynthetic stems"); sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.spines.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 480, Cercidium floridum: branches with short simple spines; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 427): rudimentary branchlets become spines.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves alternate (or clustered at the nodes), as in the genus.

traits.leaf_division.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426), Cercidium floridum: leaves evidently bipinnate.

traits.division_pattern.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426), Cercidium floridum: leaves evidently bipinnate.

traits.division_order.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426), Cercidium floridum: bipinnate: divided twice.

traits.pinnae.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 480, Cercidium floridum: primary rachis 1-2 cm. long, with 2 pinnae.

traits.leaflets.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 480, Cercidium floridum: leaflets mostly 2 or 3 pairs on each pinna; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426) give 1-3 pairs, kept as the low.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 480, Cercidium floridum: leaflets in pairs, even-pinnate.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426), Cercidium floridum: leaflets 4-8 mm long (Abrams 1944 p. 480: 4-7 mm).

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "pinnately compound leaves are about 1 inch (2.5 cm) long".

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 480, Cercidium floridum: leaflets oblong-oblanceolate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaflets entire, as in the genus.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 479, Cercidium: flowers in short corymbose clusters.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "Inflorescences of blue paloverde are 1.5 to 4.7 inches (4-12 cm) long".

traits.flower_colour.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426), Cercidium floridum: flowers bright yellow, all the petals alike; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 479, Cercidium: petals 5, yellow.

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "The fruits are flat legumes".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "flat legumes, 1.5 to 4 inches (4-10 cm) long".

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 480, Cercidium floridum: pods flat, about 1 cm. wide.

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "flowers sporadically after rains from late March to May"; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426): April and May.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "Fruits mature about 1 month after flowering, typically from May to July".

traits.leaf_out_months.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "Leaves are produced between mid-July and late November, depending on the summer rains".

traits.elevation_min_m.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "found at elevations from sea level to 4,000 feet (0-1,220 m)".

traits.elevation_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "found at elevations from sea level to 4,000 feet (0-1,220 m)"; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426): 3,500 feet or lower.

traits.light.note: FEIS species review, Parkinsonia florida (Pavek 1994): "a major component in creosotebush ... and white bursage ... climax communities on lower bajadas": open desert scrub.

traits.moisture.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426), Cercidium floridum: along washes and on flood plains, where runoff gathers in the desert.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low-branched, multi-stemmed tree with smooth blue-green bark on trunk and twigs, a sparse spreading crown of tiny leaflets, smothered in bright yellow flowers in spring. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

generator.params.note: Set by hand for blue palo verde from its sources and the photos the traits cite, on the template of foothill palo verde (parkinsonia-microphylla); the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 5.0 m tall at 40 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows on a Sonoran Desert bajada. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada, Tucson Mountain District, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles (1942) and Abrams, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos, drawing values from the library's rules for the form.
